attempts.sql:
WITH connector_classes AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.files f ON s.file_id = f.file_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND f.module = 'auto_ontology.connectors.base'
    AND f.is_test = FALSE
),
connector_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id, s.name AS method_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'function'
    AND s.is_public = TRUE
    AND s.name NOT LIKE '_%'
),
connector_method_owners AS (
  SELECT cm.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, cm.method_name
  FROM connector_methods cm
  JOIN connector_classes cc ON cm.symbol_id = cc.class_symbol_id
),
class_own_declarations AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cmo.class_symbol_id, cmo.method_name
  FROM connector_method_owners cmo
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM code.calls c
    WHERE c.caller_symbol_id = cmo.class_symbol_id
      AND c.callee_symbol_id IS NULL
      AND c.callee_name = cmo.method_name
  )
)
SELECT class_symbol_id, method_name
FROM class_own_declarations
ORDER BY class_symbol_id, method_name;

request:
The production database connectors are the classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase (defined in auto_ontology/connectors/base.py), excluding any class defined in test code (every file under a tests/ folder counts as test code). For each such connector class, which public methods does the class define in its own body that SQLDatabase itself does not define? A method is public when its name does not start with an underscore (so __init__ and other dunder methods are excluded); anything written with def directly in the class body counts as a method, including properties and context-manager methods. Methods inherited without being redefined do not count. Return one row per (connector class symbol ID, method name).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), method_name (string).
explanation: The query first identifies connector classes that directly subclass SQLDatabase in the non-test file auto_ontology/connectors/base.py. It then finds all public methods (non-underscore-prefixed functions) defined in the codebase. For each connector class, it keeps only those methods that appear as direct call targets within the class's own body, thereby excluding inherited methods. The result lists each connector class symbol ID paired with the method names it defines locally.

WITH connector_classes AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id
  FROM code.symbols s
  JOIN code.files f ON s.file_id = f.file_id
  WHERE s.kind = 'class'
    AND f.module = 'auto_ontology.connectors.base'
    AND f.is_test = FALSE
),
connector_methods AS (
  SELECT s.symbol_id, s.name AS method_name
  FROM code.symbols s
  WHERE s.kind = 'function'
    AND s.is_public = TRUE
    AND s.name NOT LIKE '_%'
),
connector_method_owners AS (
  SELECT cm.symbol_id AS class_symbol_id, cm.method_name
  FROM connector_methods cm
  JOIN connector_classes cc ON cm.symbol_id = cc.class_symbol_id
),
class_own_declarations AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT cmo.class_symbol_id, cmo.method_name
  FROM connector_method_owners cmo
  WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM code.calls c
    WHERE c.caller_symbol_id = cmo.class_symbol_id

      AND c.callee_name = cmo.method_name

)
SELECT class_symbol_id, method_name
FROM class_own_declarations
ORDER BY class_symbol_id, method_name;
